Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

SIMP 0.3.0

  • Step-adapted minimum-error integrators. simp_b_optimal() returns the multistage coefficients that minimize the worst-case energy error a splitting integrator induces on a harmonic (Gaussian) target across a band of dimensionless steps (0, nu_max], where nu_max = omega_max * eps follows from the highest target frequency (the largest mass-scaled Hessian eigenvalue). simp_integrate() and simp_hmc() take integrator = "adaptive2" / "adaptive3" with nu_max to use the tuned two- or three-stage scheme. Exposed in C++ as simp::two_stage_adaptive / simp::three_stage_adaptive in <simp/adapt.h>.
  • Exact harmonic energy-error analysis backing the adaptation, in <simp/harmonic.h>: simp::harmonic_energy_error(scheme, nu) is the relative energy-oscillation amplitude the scheme induces on the unit oscillator at dimensionless step nu, and simp::harmonic_stability_limit(scheme) is the largest stable step. Both come from the scheme’s exact 2x2 propagation matrix and its invariant quadratic form.
  • Parametric multistage constructors simp::two_stage(b) and simp::three_stage(b, a) in <simp/scheme.h>; minerror2() is now the b = (3 - sqrt(5)) / 4 member of two_stage.
  • simp_integrate_mts() advances a split potential U = U_slow + U_fast with the multiple-time-stepping (RESPA / Verlet-I) integrator: the slow force is evaluated once per outer step while the fast force drives m inner substeps, so a stiff-but-cheap part takes small steps without the expensive part paying the same rate. Exposed in C++ as simp::step_mts / simp::integrate_mts in <simp/mts.h>.

SIMP 0.2.0

  • New integrator "minerror2": a two-stage order-two scheme whose free kick weight is fixed at (3 - sqrt(5)) / 4, the value that cancels the leading energy-error term on a harmonic (Gaussian) target. It takes two gradient evaluations per step, conserves energy far better than leapfrog near a Gaussian, and admits larger steps without the stability cliff of the high-order composition schemes.
  • simp_integrate_nonsep() integrates non-separable Hamiltonians (for example Riemannian dynamics with a position-dependent mass) with the generalized (implicit) leapfrog, exposed in C++ as simp::step_implicit in <simp/implicit.h>. For a separable Hamiltonian it reduces to leapfrog.
  • Recovery tests cover the new members: the minerror2 energy cancellation and its order on a nonlinear problem, and the generalized leapfrog’s separable-reduction, energy conservation, and reversibility.

SIMP 0.1.0

First release of SIMP as a symplectic-integration library.

  • simp_integrate() advances a separable Hamiltonian system with a chosen symplectic splitting scheme, returning the endpoint or the full trajectory and, optionally, the total energy along it.
  • simp_schemes() lists the built-in integrators: leapfrog and the Yoshida order 4, 6, and 8 members, generated from leapfrog by triple-jump composition.
  • simp_hmc() runs Hamiltonian Monte Carlo with any of the schemes.
  • Header-only, scalar-templated C++ core in inst/include/simp/ for LinkingTo: SIMP consumers.
